summary_paragraph: The patient, a homeless man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and recent toe amputations due to frostbite, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and left foot pain. He had not taken his torsemide due to lack of access, leading to an acute exacerbation of heart failure, confirmed by elevated proBNP and clinical findings. He also had symptoms and lab findings consistent with a COPD exacerbation, treated with levofloxacin and prednisone. A syncopal event occurred during hospitalization, resulting in a head strike; CT showed a scalp hematoma but no intracranial bleed, with incidental note of a slowly growing scalp mass requiring follow-up imaging. Podiatry found no active foot infection. Social work assisted with housing and medication access. He improved with diuresis and respiratory treatment, was discharged home with a month’s medication supply, and follow-up arranged for primary care, podiatry, and imaging.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
